subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 4: Electricity: Magnetic and Heating Effects
central_question: How does electric current produce magnetic fields and heat, and how do chemical cells and batteries supply current for practical devices?
in_scope_units: Magnetic effect of current and compass deflection.
Electromagnets, poles, iron cores, strength, current direction and lifting applications.
Heating effect, resistance, nichrome, heating elements and electrical safety.
Voltaic cells, electrodes, electrolytes and lemon-cell construction.
Dry cells, rechargeable batteries, battery life, recycling and emerging battery technologies.
banned_topics: Household wiring calculations and Ohm's law.
Chemical electrochemistry beyond the cell descriptions in the chapter.

known_pitfalls.claim: A wire remains magnetic after current is switched off.
known_pitfalls.correction: The magnetic field around the wire or coil disappears when current stops.

known_pitfalls.claim: An iron core is required for any coil to show magnetic effect.
known_pitfalls.correction: A current-carrying coil already produces a magnetic field; an iron core makes it stronger.

known_pitfalls.claim: More current only strengthens magnetism and does not affect heating.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter shows both stronger magnetic effect and greater heating when current increases.

known_pitfalls.claim: Nichrome is used because it offers no resistance.
known_pitfalls.correction: Nichrome has higher resistance than comparable copper wire, converting more electrical energy into heat.

known_pitfalls.claim: All batteries can be recharged indefinitely.
known_pitfalls.correction: Dry cells are single-use, and rechargeable batteries also wear out after many cycles.

recommended_example_progression: Use Activity 4.1 to connect current with compass deflection.
Use Activities 4.2–4.4 to construct and test an electromagnet.
Use Activity 4.5 to investigate heating in nichrome.
Use Activity 4.6 to construct a lemon-cell battery and test LED polarity.
Use Keep the curiosity alive Q8–Q11 to integrate magnetism, heating and cells.
